summary: A rectangle revolved about an oblique axis parallel to two of its edges. The coordinates are the issue's, rounded to 9 decimals, so the 'parallel' edges are off by about 1e-10.

cases.name: revolve_rect_oblique_axis_90
cases.note: A 10 x 3 rectangle revolved 90 degrees about an axis at 30 degrees in its plane, parallel to two of its edges; coordinates rounded to 9 decimals and the direction to 12, so the 'parallel' edges are off by about 1e-10. Exact intent (rectangle 10 x 3, edges 2 and 5 from the axis): 30 x 3.5 x pi/2 = 164.933614313; the rounding moves it by 4e-11 relative. Area: each lateral face is edge length x its midpoint's distance from the axis x pi/2 (Pappus), plus the two caps (2 x 29.999999997): 202.942465739. Faces: 6 geometric faces (2 cylinders, from the axis-parallel edges at 2 and 5 mm; 2 planes, from the edges perpendicular to the axis; 2 caps). Not an exact expectation: a kernel may split a face at its seam. SolidCraft's STEP writer turned the two near-cylinders into cones with a semi-angle of 8e-12 rad; the kernel-side check is that the revolve itself is closed with this volume.

volume.formula: Pappus, from the typed coordinates (shoelace area and centroid, double precision): area 29.999999997344, centroid 3.500000000180 from the axis, volume = area x distance x pi/2 = 164.933614307.
